claim: Voluntary carbon credit retirements 2025: 202 MtCO2e (includes some compliance transfers), value just over USD 1.4 billion, MSCI average price USD 3.5/t vs USD 4.3 in 2024
caveats: Includes some compliance transfers; MSCI average price across voluntary transactions.
title: Carbon Credits Come of Age in 2025

claim: Google agreed to buy 1 million AWD rice credits from Mitti Labs through 2030; 70,000+ farmers targeted; about 100,000 ha at peak delivery across Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana; financial terms undisclosed
caveats: Target delivery through 2030; farmer count and hectare figures are target figures reported by developer; financial terms undisclosed.
title: Google Agrees to Buy 1 Million Carbon Credits from Mitti Labs

claim: India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme: compliance obligations in force for seven sectors (aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp and paper, petroleum refining, petrochemicals, textiles); about 490 entities; first compliance date 31 July for FY2025-26
caveats: Covers ~490 designated consumers under Bureau of Energy Efficiency / Ministry of Power regulations; first compliance date 31 July FY2025-26.
title: Compliance obligations under India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme enter force for seven sectors

claim: Initial Indian carbon credit price expected around USD 10/tCO2e (government and industry estimates)
caveats: Pre-trading estimate based on industry surveys and Bureau of Energy Efficiency benchmark indications; actual market clearing price will vary.
title: Industry sees initial carbon credits priced around $10/mtCO2e in India

claim: Indian regenerative-agriculture credits offered at EUR 15 to 27/t
caveats: Observed market ask prices for certified regenerative agriculture and soil carbon credits in India.
title: Carbon Credit Price Guide

claim: Indigo Ag pays farmers USD 15 per tonne CO2e stored
caveats: US soil carbon programme pricing structure; referenced as international benchmark only; not an Indian market promise.
title: Will Carbon Farming Pay Off for Farmers?

claim: Verra VM0051 launched early 2025; ICAO approval for CORSIA; eight registered projects with an estimated 1.73 million credits a year
caveats: VM0051 replaces and updates previous rice methodologies; CORSIA Phase 1 eligibility granted by ICAO Technical Advisory Body.
title: Verra's VM0051 Gains CORSIA Eligibility Boosting Rice Carbon Credit Demand

claim: Varaha: Mirova investing USD 30.5M for a share of future credits; Kheti project over 200,000 ha, target 675,000 ha, roughly 337,000 farmers expected at scale
caveats: Company stated targets; investment is pre-financing against anticipated future credit delivery from regenerative agriculture.
title: Kering-backed fund Mirova pours $30.5M into India's Varaha for regenerative farming push

claim: About 86% of Indian operational holdings are under 2 ha; average holding 1.08 ha (2015-16); small and marginal holdings hold about 47% of operated area
caveats: Official Government of India Agriculture Census 2015-16 data. Operational holdings under 2 hectares classify as marginal (<1 ha) and small (1-2 ha).
publisher: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Agriculture Census
title: Major Current Trends in Fragmentation of Land Holdings in Indian Agriculture

claim: Indian agriculture emitted about 0.73 Gt CO2e in 2021 (12.7% of global agricultural emissions); rice cultivation 96.7 Mt CO2e
caveats: Emissions estimated based on IPCC guidelines. Rice cultivation methane emissions converted at standard AR5 GWP100.
title: India's Agriculture Sector Produced 12.7% of Global Agricultural CO2e Emissions in 2021

claim: Agriculture accounts for more than 70% of global water withdrawals
caveats: Global freshwater withdrawal percentage across surface and groundwater systems.
publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
title: The State of Food and Agriculture 2020: Overcoming water challenges in agriculture

claim: AWD can reduce irrigation water use by roughly 15 to 30% and methane by roughly 30 to 70% without reducing yields when done as recommended (ranges vary by study; cite the primary studies and IRRI guidance)
caveats: Ranges documented across multi-site field trials by IRRI and IWMI. Yield neutral when safe AWD threshold (water table <= 15cm below soil surface before re-flooding) is observed.
title: Explainer: Alternate Wetting and Drying Irrigation Technique

claim: Agriculture uses about 17 to 20% of India's electricity; 30 to 32 million irrigation pump sets, nearly two-thirds electric
caveats: Electricity consumption proportion varies by state (higher in Punjab, Haryana, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh). Remainder of pump sets operate on diesel.
title: Agriculture Sector Energy Transition and Policy Assessment

claim: Stubble burning contributed 40% of Delhi's PM2.5 on 1 Nov 2020 (SAFAR)
caveats: Single-day peak contribution estimated by SAFAR (Ministry of Earth Sciences) atmospheric transport model during post-monsoon harvest.
title: At 40%, Stubble Burning Contribution in Delhi's Pollution Soars to Season's High

caveats: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data reported by National Statistical Office / analyzed by SBI Economic Research.
title: Periodic Labour Force Survey Economic Insights

claim: Average monthly income of rural households Rs 12,698 in 2021-22, up from Rs 8,059 in 2016-17
caveats: NABARD All India Rural Financial Inclusion Survey (NAFIS) 2021-22. Nominal figures across agricultural and non-agricultural rural households.
title: Average monthly income of rural households goes up by over 57% between 2016-17 and 2021-22
